specimen_collector_sample_id.title: ID du collecteur d’échantillons
specimen_collector_sample_id.description: Nom défini par l’utilisateur pour l’échantillon
comments: Conservez l’ID de l’échantillon du collecteur. Si ce numéro est considéré comme une information identifiable, fournissez un autre identifiant. Assurez-vous de conserver la clé qui correspond aux identifiants d’origine et alternatifs aux fins de traçabilité et de suivi, au besoin. Chaque ID d’échantillon de collecteur provenant d’un seul demandeur doit être unique. Il peut avoir n’importe quel format, mais nous vous suggérons de le rendre concis, unique et cohérent au sein de votre laboratoire.

third_party_lab_service_provider_name.title: Nom du fournisseur de services de laboratoire tiers
third_party_lab_service_provider_name.description: Nom de la société ou du laboratoire tiers qui fournit les services
comments: Indiquez le nom complet et non abrégé de l’entreprise ou du laboratoire.

third_party_lab_sample_id.title: ID de l’échantillon de laboratoire tiers
third_party_lab_sample_id.description: Identifiant attribué à un échantillon par un prestataire de services tiers
comments: Conservez l’identifiant de l’échantillon fourni par le prestataire de services tiers.

case_id.title: ID du dossier
case_id.description: Identifiant utilisé pour désigner un cas de maladie détecté sur le plan épidémiologique
comments: Fournissez l’identifiant du cas, lequel facilite grandement le lien entre les données de laboratoire et les données épidémiologiques. Il peut être considéré comme une information identifiable. Consultez l’intendant des données avant de le transmettre.

related_specimen_primary_id.title: ID principal de l’échantillon associé
related_specimen_primary_id.description: Identifiant principal d’un échantillon associé précédemment soumis au dépôt
comments: Conservez l’identifiant primaire de l’échantillon correspondant précédemment soumis au Laboratoire national de microbiologie afin que les échantillons puissent être liés et suivis dans le système.

irida_sample_name.title: Nom de l’échantillon IRIDA
irida_sample_name.description: Identifiant attribué à un isolat séquencé dans IRIDA
comments: Enregistrez le nom de l’échantillon IRIDA, lequel sera créé par la personne saisissant les données dans la plateforme connexe. Les échantillons IRIDA peuvent être liés à des métadonnées et à des données de séquence, ou simplement à des métadonnées. Il est recommandé que le nom de l’échantillon IRIDA soit identique ou contienne l’ID de l’échantillon du collecteur pour assurer une meilleure traçabilité. Il est également recommandé que le nom de l’échantillon IRIDA reflète l’accès à GISAID. Les noms d’échantillons IRIDA ne peuvent pas contenir de barres obliques. Celles-ci doivent être remplacées par des traits de soulignement. Consultez la documentation IRIDA pour en savoir plus sur les caractères spéciaux (https://irida.corefacility.ca/documentation/user/user/samples/#adding-a-new-sample).

umbrella_bioproject_accession.title: Numéro d’accès au bioprojet cadre
umbrella_bioproject_accession.description: Numéro d’accès à INSDC attribué au bioprojet cadre pour l’effort canadien de séquençage du SRAS-CoV-2
comments: Enregistrez le numéro d’accès au bioprojet cadre en le sélectionnant à partir de la liste déroulante du modèle. Ce numéro sera identique pour tous les soumissionnaires du RCanGéCO. Différentes provinces auront leurs propres bioprojets, mais ces derniers seront liés sous un seul bioprojet cadre.

bioproject_accession.title: Numéro d’accès au bioprojet
bioproject_accession.description: Numéro d’accès à INSDC du bioprojet auquel appartient un échantillon biologique
comments: Enregistrez le numéro d’accès au bioprojet. Les bioprojets sont un outil d’organisation qui relie les données de séquence brutes, les assemblages et leurs métadonnées associées. Chaque province se verra attribuer un numéro d’accès différent au bioprojet par le Laboratoire national de microbiologie. Un numéro d’accès valide au bioprojet du NCBI contient le préfixe PRJN (p. ex., PRJNA12345); il est créé une fois au début d’un nouveau projet de séquençage.

biosample_accession.title: Numéro d’accès à un échantillon biologique
biosample_accession.description: Identifiant attribué à un échantillon biologique dans les archives INSDC
comments: Conservez le numéro d’accès renvoyé avec la soumission d’un échantillon biologique. Les échantillons biologiques de NCBI seront assortis du SAMN.

sra_accession.title: Numéro d’accès à l’archive des séquences
sra_accession.description: Identifiant de l’archive des séquences reliant les données de séquences brutes de lecture, les métadonnées méthodologiques et les mesures de contrôle de la qualité soumises à INSDC
comments: Conservez le numéro d’accès attribué au « cycle » soumis. Les accès NCBI-SRA commencent par SRR.

genbank_accession.title: Numéro d’accès à GenBank
genbank_accession.description: Identifiant GenBank attribué à la séquence dans les archives INSDC
comments: Conservez le numéro d’accès renvoyé avec la soumission de GenBank (assemblage du génome viral).

gisaid_accession.title: Numéro d’accès à la GISAID
gisaid_accession.description: Numéro d’accès à la GISAID attribué à la séquence
comments: Conservez le numéro d’accès renvoyé avec la soumission de la GISAID.

sample_collected_by.title: Échantillon prélevé par
sample_collected_by.description: Nom de l’organisme ayant prélevé l’échantillon original
comments: Le nom du collecteur d’échantillons doit être écrit au long (à quelques exceptions près) et être cohérent dans plusieurs soumissions, par exemple Agence de la santé publique du Canada, Santé publique Ontario, Centre de contrôle des maladies de la Colombie-Britannique.

examples.value: Centre de contrôle des maladies de la Colombie-Britannique

sample_collector_contact_email.title: Adresse courriel du collecteur d’échantillons
sample_collector_contact_email.description: Adresse courriel de la personne-ressource responsable du suivi concernant l’échantillon
comments: L’adresse courriel peut représenter une personne ou un laboratoire spécifique (p. ex., johnnyblogs@lab.ca, or RespLab@lab.ca).

sample_collector_contact_address.title: Adresse du collecteur d’échantillons
sample_collector_contact_address.description: Adresse postale de l’organisme soumettant l’échantillon
comments: Le format de l’adresse postale doit être le suivant : Numéro et nom de la rue, ville, province/territoire, code postal et pays.

sequence_submitted_by.title: Séquence soumise par
sequence_submitted_by.description: Nom de l’organisme ayant généré la séquence
comments: Le nom de l’agence doit être écrit au long (à quelques exceptions près) et être cohérent dans plusieurs soumissions. Si vous soumettez des échantillons plutôt que des données de séquençage, veuillez inscrire « Laboratoire national de microbiologie (LNM) ».

sequence_submitter_contact_email.title: Adresse courriel du soumissionnaire de séquence
sequence_submitter_contact_email.description: Adresse courriel de la personne-ressource responsable du suivi concernant l’échantillon
comments: L’adresse courriel peut représenter une personne ou un laboratoire spécifique (p. ex., johnnyblogs@lab.ca, or RespLab@lab.ca).

sequence_submitter_contact_address.title: Adresse du soumissionnaire de séquence
sequence_submitter_contact_address.description: Adresse postale de l’organisme soumettant l’échantillon
comments: Le format de l’adresse postale doit être le suivant : Numéro et nom de la rue, ville, province/territoire, code postal et pays.

sample_collection_date.title: Date de prélèvement de l’échantillon
sample_collection_date.description: Date à laquelle l’échantillon a été prélevé
comments: La date de prélèvement des échantillons est essentielle pour la surveillance et de nombreux types d’analyses. La granularité requise comprend l’année, le mois et le jour. Si cette date est considérée comme un renseignement identifiable, il est acceptable d’y ajouter une « gigue » en ajoutant ou en soustrayant un jour civil. La « date de réception » peut également servir de date de rechange. La date doit être fournie selon le format standard ISO 8601 : « AAAA-MM-JJ ».

sample_collection_date_precision.title: Précision de la date de prélèvement de l’échantillon
sample_collection_date_precision.description: Précision avec laquelle la « date de prélèvement de l’échantillon » a été fournie
comments: Fournissez la précision de la granularité au « jour », au « mois » ou à « l’année » pour la date fournie dans le champ « Date de prélèvement de l’échantillon ». Cette date sera tronquée selon la précision spécifiée lors de l’exportation : « jour » pour « AAAA-MM-JJ », « mois » pour « AAAA-MM » ou « année » pour « AAAA ».

sample_received_date.title: Date de réception de l’échantillon
sample_received_date.description: Date à laquelle l’échantillon a été reçu
comments: La date doit être fournie selon le format standard ISO 8601 : « AAAA-MM-JJ ».

comments: Fournissez le nom du pays à partir du vocabulaire contrôlé fourni.

geo_loc_name_state_province_territory.description: Province ou territoire où l’échantillon a été prélevé
comments: Fournissez le nom de la province ou du territoire à partir du vocabulaire contrôlé fourni.

geo_loc_name_city.description: Ville où l’échantillon a été prélevé
comments: Fournissez le nom de la ville. Utilisez ce service de recherche pour trouver le terme normalisé : https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/gaz.

organism.title: Organisme
comments: Utilisez « coronavirus du syndrome respiratoire aigu sévère 2 ». Cette valeur est fournie dans le modèle.

examples.value: Coronavirus du syndrome respiratoire aigu sévère 2

isolate.title: Isolat
comments: Fournissez le nom du virus de la GISAID, qui doit être écrit dans le format « hCov-19/CANADA/code ISO provincial à 2 chiffres-xxxxx/année ».

purpose_of_sampling.title: Objectif de l’échantillonnage
comments: La raison pour laquelle un échantillon a été prélevé peut fournir des renseignements sur les biais potentiels de la stratégie d’échantillonnage. Choisissez l’objectif de l’échantillonnage à partir de la liste déroulante du modèle. Il est très probable que l’échantillon ait été prélevé en vue d’un test diagnostique. La raison pour laquelle un échantillon a été prélevé à l’origine peut différer de la raison pour laquelle il a été sélectionné aux fins de séquençage, ce qui doit être indiqué dans le champ « Objectif du séquençage ».

purpose_of_sampling_details.title: Détails de l’objectif de l’échantillonnage
purpose_of_sampling_details.description: Détails précis concernant le motif de prélèvement de l’échantillon
comments: Fournissez une description détaillée de la raison pour laquelle l’échantillon a été prélevé en utilisant du texte libre. La description peut inclure l’importance de l’échantillon pour une enquête, une activité de surveillance ou une question de recherche particulière dans le domaine de la santé publique. Si les détails ne sont pas disponibles, fournissez une valeur nulle.

examples.value: L’échantillon a été prélevé pour étudier la prévalence des variants associés à la transmission du vison à l’homme au Canada.

nml_submitted_specimen_type.title: Type d’échantillon soumis au LNM
nml_submitted_specimen_type.description: Type d’échantillon soumis au Laboratoire national de microbiologie (LNM) aux fins d’analyse
comments: Ces renseignements sont requis pour le téléchargement à l’aide du système LaSER du RCRSP. Choisissez le type d’échantillon à partir de la liste de sélection fournie. Si les données de séquences sont soumises plutôt qu’un échantillon aux fins d’analyse, sélectionnez « Sans objet ».

related_specimen_relationship_type.title: Type de relation de l’échantillon lié
related_specimen_relationship_type.description: Relation entre l’échantillon actuel et celui précédemment soumis au dépôt
comments: Fournissez l’étiquette qui décrit comment l’échantillon précédent est lié à l’échantillon actuel soumis à partir de la liste de sélection fournie afin que les échantillons puissent être liés et suivis dans le système.

Si aucun des processus de la liste de sélection ne s’applique, inscrivez « Sans objet ».

purpose_of_sequencing.title: Objectif du séquençage
purpose_of_sequencing.description: Raison pour laquelle l’échantillon a été séquencé
comments: La raison pour laquelle un échantillon a été initialement prélevé peut différer de la raison pour laquelle il a été sélectionné aux fins de séquençage. La raison pour laquelle un échantillon a été séquencé peut fournir des renseignements sur les biais potentiels dans la stratégie de séquençage. Fournissez le but du séquençage à partir de la liste de sélection dans le modèle. Le motif de prélèvement de l’échantillon doit être indiqué dans le champ « Objectif de l’échantillonnage ».

purpose_of_sequencing_details.title: Détails de l’objectif du séquençage
purpose_of_sequencing_details.description: Description de la raison pour laquelle l’échantillon a été séquencé, fournissant des détails spécifiques
comments: Fournissez une description détaillée de la raison pour laquelle l’échantillon a été séquencé en utilisant du texte libre. La description peut inclure l’importance des séquences pour une enquête, une activité de surveillance ou une question de recherche particulière dans le domaine de la santé publique. Les descriptions normalisées suggérées sont les suivantes : Dépistage de l’absence de détection du gène S (abandon du gène S), dépistage de variants associés aux visons, dépistage du variant B.1.1.7, dépistage du variant B.1.135, dépistage du variant P.1, dépistage en raison des antécédents de voyage, dépistage en raison d’un contact étroit avec une personne infectée, évaluation des mesures de contrôle de la santé publique, détermination des introductions et de la propagation précoces, enquête sur les expositions liées aux voyages aériens, enquête sur les travailleurs étrangers temporaires, enquête sur les régions éloignées, enquête sur les travailleurs de la santé, enquête sur les écoles et les universités, enquête sur la réinfection.

Le séquençage a été effectué à l’aide d’un instrument de séquençage <à remplir>. Les bibliothèques ont été préparées à l’aide de la trousse <à remplir>. »

Be sure to store the key that maps between the original and alternative IDs for traceability and follow up if necessary. Every collector sample ID from a single submitter must be unique. It can have any format, but we suggest that you make it concise, unique and consistent within your lab.

Slots.name: third_party_lab_service_provider_name
Slots.title: third party lab service provider name
Slots.description: The name of the third party company or laboratory that provided services.
Slots.comments: Provide the full, unabbreviated name of the company or laboratory.

Slots.name: third_party_lab_sample_id
Slots.title: third party lab sample ID
Slots.description: The identifier assigned to a sample by a third party service provider.
Slots.comments: Store the sample identifier supplied by the third party services provider.

Slots.name: case_id
Slots.title: case ID
Slots.description: The identifier used to specify an epidemiologically detected case of disease.
Slots.comments: Provide the case identifer. The case ID greatly facilitates linkage between laboratory and epidemiological data. The case ID may be considered identifiable information. Consult the data steward before sharing.

Slots.name: related_specimen_primary_id
Slots.title: Related specimen primary ID
Slots.description: The primary ID of a related specimen previously submitted to the repository.
Slots.comments: Store the primary ID of the related specimen previously submitted to the National Microbiology Laboratory so that the samples can be linked and tracked through the system.

Slots.name: irida_sample_name
Slots.title: IRIDA sample name
Slots.description: The identifier assigned to a sequenced isolate in IRIDA.
Slots.comments: Store the IRIDA sample name. The IRIDA sample name will be created by the individual entering data into the IRIDA platform. IRIDA samples may be linked to metadata and sequence data, or just metadata alone. It is recommended that the IRIDA sample name be the same as, or contain, the specimen collector sample ID for better traceability. It is also recommended that the IRIDA sample name mirror the GISAID accession. IRIDA sample names cannot contain slashes. Slashes should be replaced by underscores. See IRIDA documentation for more information regarding special characters (https://irida.corefacility.ca/documentation/user/user/samples/#adding-a-new-sample).

Slots.name: umbrella_bioproject_accession
Slots.title: umbrella bioproject accession
Slots.description: The INSDC accession number assigned to the umbrella BioProject for the Canadian SARS-CoV-2 sequencing effort.
Slots.comments: Store the umbrella BioProject accession by selecting it from the picklist in the template. The umbrella BioProject accession will be identical for all CanCOGen submitters. Different provinces will have their own BioProjects, however these BioProjects will be linked under one umbrella BioProject.

Slots.name: bioproject_accession
Slots.title: bioproject accession
Slots.description: The INSDC accession number of the BioProject(s) to which the BioSample belongs.
Slots.comments: Store the BioProject accession number. BioProjects are an organizing tool that links together raw sequence data, assemblies, and their associated metadata. Each province will be assigned a different bioproject accession number by the National Microbiology Lab. A valid NCBI BioProject accession has prefix PRJN e.g., PRJNA12345, and is created once at the beginning of a new sequencing project.

Slots.name: biosample_accession
Slots.title: biosample accession
Slots.description: The identifier assigned to a BioSample in INSDC archives.
Slots.comments: Store the accession returned from the BioSample submission. NCBI BioSamples will have the prefix SAMN.

Slots.name: sra_accession
Slots.title: SRA accession
Slots.description: The Sequence Read Archive (SRA) identifier linking raw read data, methodological metadata and quality control metrics submitted to the INSDC.
Slots.comments: Store the accession assigned to the submitted "run". NCBI-SRA accessions start with SRR.

Slots.name: genbank_accession
Slots.title: GenBank accession
Slots.description: The GenBank identifier assigned to the sequence in the INSDC archives.
Slots.comments: Store the accession returned from a GenBank submission (viral genome assembly).

Slots.name: gisaid_accession
Slots.title: GISAID accession
Slots.description: The GISAID accession number assigned to the sequence.
Slots.comments: Store the accession returned from the GISAID submission.

Slots.name: sample_collected_by
Slots.title: sample collected by
Slots.description: The name of the agency that collected the original sample.
Slots.comments: The name of the sample collector should be written out in full, (with minor exceptions) and be consistent across multple submissions e.g. Public Health Agency of Canada, Public Health Ontario, BC Centre for Disease Control. The sample collector specified is at the discretion of the data provider (i.e. may be hospital, provincial public health lab, or other).

Slots.name: sample_collector_contact_email
Slots.title: sample collector contact email
Slots.description: The email address of the contact responsible for follow-up regarding the sample.
Slots.comments: The email address can represent a specific individual or lab e.g. johnnyblogs@lab.ca, or RespLab@lab.ca

Slots.name: sample_collector_contact_address
Slots.title: sample collector contact address
Slots.description: The mailing address of the agency submitting the sample.
Slots.comments: The mailing address should be in the format: Street number and name, City, Province/Territory, Postal Code, Country
Slots.examples: 655 Lab St, Vancouver, British Columbia, V5N 2A2, Canada

Slots.name: sequence_submitted_by
Slots.title: sequence submitted by
Slots.description: The name of the agency that generated the sequence.
Slots.comments: The name of the agency should be written out in full, (with minor exceptions) and be consistent across multple submissions. If submitting specimens rather than sequencing data, please put the "National Microbiology Laboratory (NML)".

Slots.name: sequence_submitter_contact_email
Slots.title: sequence submitter contact email
Slots.description: The email address of the contact responsible for follow-up regarding the sequence.
Slots.comments: The email address can represent a specific individual or lab e.g. johnnyblogs@lab.ca, or RespLab@lab.ca

Slots.name: sequence_submitter_contact_address
Slots.title: sequence submitter contact address
Slots.description: The mailing address of the agency submitting the sequence.
Slots.comments: The mailing address should be in the format: Street number and name, City, Province/Territory, Postal Code, Country
Slots.examples: 123 Sunnybrooke St, Toronto, Ontario, M4P 1L6, Canada

Slots.name: sample_collection_date
Slots.title: sample collection date
Slots.description: The date on which the sample was collected.
Slots.comments: Sample collection date is critical for surveillance and many types of analyses. Required granularity includes year, month and day. If this date is considered identifiable information, it is acceptable to add "jitter" by adding or subtracting a calendar day (acceptable by GISAID). Alternatively, ”received date” may be used as a substitute. The date should be provided in ISO 8601 standard format "YYYY-MM-DD".

Slots.name: sample_collection_date_precision
Slots.title: sample collection date precision
Slots.description: The precision to which the "sample collection date" was provided.
Slots.comments: Provide the precision of granularity to the "day", "month", or "year" for the date provided in the "sample collection date" field. The "sample collection date" will be truncated to the precision specified upon export: "day" for "YYYY-MM-DD", "month" for "YYYY-MM", or "year" for "YYYY".

Slots.name: sample_received_date
Slots.title: sample received date
Slots.description: The date on which the sample was received.
Slots.comments: ISO 8601 standard "YYYY-MM-DD".

Slots.name: geo_loc_name_country
Slots.title: geo_loc_name (country)
Slots.description: The country where the sample was collected.
Slots.comments: Provide the country name from the controlled vocabulary provided.

Slots.name: geo_loc_name_state_province_territory
Slots.title: geo_loc_name (state/province/territory)
Slots.description: The province/territory where the sample was collected.
Slots.comments: Provide the province/territory name from the controlled vocabulary provided.

Slots.name: geo_loc_name_city
Slots.title: geo_loc_name (city)
Slots.description: The city where the sample was collected.
Slots.comments: Provide the city name. Use this look-up service to identify the standardized term: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/gaz

Slots.name: organism
Slots.title: organism
Slots.description: Taxonomic name of the organism.
Slots.comments: Use "Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2". This value is provided in the template.

Slots.name: isolate
Slots.title: isolate
Slots.description: Identifier of the specific isolate.
Slots.comments: Provide the GISAID virus name, which should be written in the format “hCov-19/CANADA/2 digit provincial ISO code-xxxxx/year”.

Slots.name: purpose_of_sampling
Slots.title: purpose of sampling
Slots.description: The reason that the sample was collected.
Slots.comments: The reason a sample was collected may provide information about potential biases in sampling strategy. Provide the purpose of sampling from the picklist in the template. Most likely, the sample was collected for diagnostic testing. The reason why a sample was originally collected may differ from the reason why it was selected for sequencing, which should be indicated in the "purpose of sequencing" field.

Slots.name: purpose_of_sampling_details
Slots.title: purpose of sampling details
Slots.description: The description of why the sample was collected, providing specific details.
Slots.comments: Provide an expanded description of why the sample was collected using free text. The description may include the importance of the sample for a particular public health investigation/surveillance activity/research question. If details are not available, provide a null value.
Slots.examples: The sample was collected to investigate the prevalence of variants associated with mink-to-human transmission in Canada.

Slots.name: nml_submitted_specimen_type
Slots.title: NML submitted specimen type
Slots.description: The type of specimen submitted to the National Microbiology Laboratory (NML) for testing.
Slots.comments: This information is required for upload through the CNPHI LaSER system. Select the specimen type from the pick list provided. If sequence data is being submitted rather than a specimen for testing, select “Not Applicable”.

Slots.name: related_specimen_relationship_type
Slots.title: Related specimen relationship type
Slots.description: The relationship of the current specimen to the specimen/sample previously submitted to the repository.
Slots.comments: Provide the tag that describes how the previous sample is related to the current sample being submitted from the pick list provided, so that the samples can be linked and tracked in the system.

Slots.name: anatomical_material
Slots.title: anatomical material
Slots.description: A substance obtained from an anatomical part of an organism e.g. tissue, blood.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if an anatomical material was sampled. Use the picklist provided in the template. If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: anatomical_part
Slots.title: anatomical part
Slots.description: An anatomical part of an organism e.g. oropharynx.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if an anatomical part was sampled. Use the picklist provided in the template. If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: body_product
Slots.title: body product
Slots.description: A substance excreted/secreted from an organism e.g. feces, urine, sweat.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if a body product was sampled. Use the picklist provided in the template.  If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: environmental_material
Slots.title: environmental material
Slots.description: A substance obtained from the natural or man-made environment e.g. soil, water, sewage.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if an environmental material was sampled. Use the picklist provided in the template.  If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: environmental_site
Slots.title: environmental site
Slots.description: An environmental location may describe a site in the natural or built environment e.g. contact surface, metal can, hospital, wet market, bat cave.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if an environmental site was sampled. Use the picklist provided in the template.  If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: collection_device
Slots.title: collection device
Slots.description: The instrument or container used to collect the sample e.g. swab.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if a device was used for sampling. Use the picklist provided in the template. If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: collection_method
Slots.title: collection method
Slots.description: The process used to collect the sample e.g. phlebotomy, necropsy.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if a collection method was used for sampling. Use the picklist provided in the template.  If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: collection_protocol
Slots.title: collection protocol
Slots.description: The name and version of a particular protocol used for sampling.
Slots.comments: Free text.

Slots.name: specimen_processing
Slots.title: specimen processing
Slots.description: Any processing applied to the sample during or after receiving the sample.
Slots.comments: Critical for interpreting data. Select all the applicable processes from the pick list. If virus was passaged, include information in "lab host", "passage number", and "passage method" fields. If none of the processes in the pick list apply, put "not applicable".

Slots.name: specimen_processing_details
Slots.title: specimen processing details
Slots.description: Detailed information regarding the processing applied to a sample during or after receiving the sample.
Slots.comments: Provide a free text description of any processing details applied to a sample.
Slots.examples: 25 swabs were pooled and further prepared as a single sample during library prep.

Slots.name: lab_host
Slots.title: lab host
Slots.description: Name and description of the laboratory host used to propagate the source organism or material from which the sample was obtained.
Slots.comments: Type of cell line used for propagation. Provide the name of the cell line using the picklist in the template. If not passaged, put "not applicable".

Slots.name: passage_number
Slots.title: passage number
Slots.description: Number of passages.
Slots.comments: Provide number of known passages. If not passaged, put "not applicable"

Slots.name: passage_method
Slots.title: passage method
Slots.description: Description of how organism was passaged.
Slots.comments: Free text. Provide a very short description (<10 words). If not passaged, put "not applicable".

Slots.name: biomaterial_extracted
Slots.title: biomaterial extracted
Slots.description: The biomaterial extracted from samples for the purpose of sequencing.
Slots.comments: Provide the biomaterial extracted from the picklist in the template.

Slots.name: host_common_name
Slots.title: host (common name)
Slots.description: The commonly used name of the host.
Slots.comments: Common name or scientific name are required if there was a host. Both can be provided, if known. Use terms from the pick lists in the template. Common name e.g. human, bat. If the sample was environmental, put "not applicable.

Slots.name: host_scientific_name
Slots.title: host (scientific name)
Slots.description: The taxonomic, or scientific name of the host.
Slots.comments: Common name or scientific name are required if there was a host. Both can be provided, if known. Use terms from the pick lists in the template. Scientific name e.g. Homo sapiens, If the sample was environmental, put "not applicable

Slots.name: host_health_state
Slots.title: host health state
Slots.description: Health status of the host at the time of sample collection.
Slots.comments: If known, select a descriptor from the pick list provided in the template.

Slots.name: host_health_status_details
Slots.title: host health status details
Slots.description: Further details pertaining to the health or disease status of the host at time of collection.
Slots.comments: If known, select a descriptor from the pick list provided in the template.

Slots.name: host_health_outcome
Slots.title: host health outcome
Slots.description: Disease outcome in the host.
Slots.comments: If known, select a descriptor from the pick list provided in the template.

Slots.name: host_disease
Slots.title: host disease
Slots.description: The name of the disease experienced by the host.
Slots.comments: Select "COVID-19" from the pick list provided in the template.

Slots.name: host_age
Slots.title: host age
Slots.description: Age of host at the time of sampling.
Slots.comments: Enter the age of the host in years. If not available, provide a null value. If there is not host, put "Not Applicable".

Slots.name: host_age_unit
Slots.title: host age unit
Slots.description: The unit used to measure the host age, in either months or years.
Slots.comments: Indicate whether the host age is in months or years. Age indicated in months will be binned to the 0 - 9 year age bin.

Slots.name: host_age_bin
Slots.title: host age bin
Slots.description: Age of host at the time of sampling, expressed as an age group.
Slots.comments: Select the corresponding host age bin from the pick list provided in the template. If not available, provide a null value.

Slots.name: host_gender
Slots.title: host gender
Slots.description: The gender of the host at the time of sample collection.
Slots.comments: Select the corresponding host gender from the pick list provided in the template. If not available, provide a null value. If there is no host, put "Not Applicable".

Slots.name: host_residence_geo_loc_name_country
Slots.title: host residence geo_loc name (country)
Slots.description: The country of residence of the host.
Slots.comments: Select the country name from pick list provided in the template.

Slots.name: host_residence_geo_loc_name_state_province_territory
Slots.title: host residence geo_loc name (state/province/territory)
Slots.description: The state/province/territory of residence of the host.
Slots.comments: Select the province/territory name from pick list provided in the template.

Slots.name: host_subject_id
Slots.title: host subject ID
Slots.description: A unique identifier by which each host can be referred to e.g. #131
Slots.comments: Provide the host identifier. Should be a unique, user-defined identifier.

Slots.name: symptom_onset_date
Slots.title: symptom onset date
Slots.description: The date on which the symptoms began or were first noted.
Slots.comments: ISO 8601 standard "YYYY-MM-DD".

Slots.name: signs_and_symptoms
Slots.title: signs and symptoms
Slots.description: A perceived change in function or sensation, (loss, disturbance or appearance) indicative of a disease, reported by a patient or clinician.
Slots.comments: Select all of the symptoms experienced by the host from the pick list.

Slots.name: preexisting_conditions_and_risk_factors
Slots.title: pre-existing conditions and risk factors
Slots.description: Patient pre-existing conditions and risk factors. <li>Pre-existing condition: A medical condition that existed prior to the current infection. <li>Risk Factor: A variable associated with an increased risk of disease or infection.
Slots.comments: Select all of the pre-existing conditions and risk factors experienced by the host from the pick list. If the desired term is missing, contact the curation team.

Slots.name: complications
Slots.title: complications
Slots.description: Patient medical complications that are believed to have occurred as a result of host disease.
Slots.comments: Select all of the complications experienced by the host from the pick list. If the desired term is missing, contact the curation team.

Slots.name: host_vaccination_status
Slots.title: host vaccination status
Slots.description: The vaccination status of the host (fully vaccinated, partially vaccinated, or not vaccinated).
Slots.comments: Select the vaccination status of the host from the pick list.

Slots.name: number_of_vaccine_doses_received
Slots.title: number of vaccine doses received
Slots.description: The number of doses of the vaccine recived by the host.
Slots.comments: Record how many doses of the vaccine the host has received.

Slots.name: vaccination_dose_1_vaccine_name
Slots.title: vaccination dose 1 vaccine name
Slots.description: The name of the vaccine administered as the first dose of a vaccine regimen.
Slots.comments: Provide the name and the corresponding manufacturer of the COVID-19 vaccine administered as the first dose by selecting a value from the pick list

Slots.name: vaccination_dose_1_vaccination_date
Slots.title: vaccination dose 1 vaccination date
Slots.description: The date the first dose of a vaccine was administered.
Slots.comments: Provide the date the first dose of COVID-19 vaccine was administered. The date should be provided in ISO 8601 standard format "YYYY-MM-DD".

Slots.name: vaccination_dose_2_vaccine_name
Slots.title: vaccination dose 2 vaccine name
Slots.description: The name of the vaccine administered as the second dose of a vaccine regimen.
Slots.comments: Provide the name and the corresponding manufacturer of the COVID-19 vaccine administered as the second dose by selecting a value from the pick list

Slots.name: vaccination_dose_2_vaccination_date
Slots.title: vaccination dose 2 vaccination date
Slots.description: The date the second dose of a vaccine was administered.
Slots.comments: Provide the date the second dose of COVID-19 vaccine was administered. The date should be provided in ISO 8601 standard format "YYYY-MM-DD".

Slots.name: vaccination_dose_3_vaccine_name
Slots.title: vaccination dose 3 vaccine name
Slots.description: The name of the vaccine administered as the third dose of a vaccine regimen.
Slots.comments: Provide the name and the corresponding manufacturer of the COVID-19 vaccine administered as the third dose by selecting a value from the pick list

Slots.name: vaccination_dose_3_vaccination_date
Slots.title: vaccination dose 3 vaccination date
Slots.description: The date the third dose of a vaccine was administered.
Slots.comments: Provide the date the third dose of COVID-19 vaccine was administered. The date should be provided in ISO 8601 standard format "YYYY-MM-DD".

Slots.name: vaccination_dose_4_vaccine_name
Slots.title: vaccination dose 4 vaccine name
Slots.description: The name of the vaccine administered as the fourth dose of a vaccine regimen.
Slots.comments: Provide the name and the corresponding manufacturer of the COVID-19 vaccine administered as the fourth dose by selecting a value from the pick list

Slots.name: vaccination_dose_4_vaccination_date
Slots.title: vaccination dose 4 vaccination date
Slots.description: The date the fourth dose of a vaccine was administered.
Slots.comments: Provide the date the fourth dose of COVID-19 vaccine was administered. The date should be provided in ISO 8601 standard format "YYYY-MM-DD".

Slots.name: vaccination_history
Slots.title: vaccination history
Slots.description: A description of the vaccines received and the administration dates of a series of vaccinations against a specific disease or a set of diseases.
Slots.comments: Free text description of the dates and vaccines administered against a particular disease/set of diseases. It is also acceptable to concatenate the individual dose information (vaccine name, vaccination date) separated by semicolons.

Slots.name: location_of_exposure_geo_loc_name_country
Slots.title: location of exposure geo_loc name (country)
Slots.description: The country where the host was likely exposed to the causative agent of the illness.
Slots.comments: Select the country name from pick list provided in the template.

Slots.name: destination_of_most_recent_travel_city
Slots.title: destination of most recent travel (city)
Slots.description: The name of the city that was the destination of most recent travel.
Slots.comments: Provide the name of the city that the host travelled to. Use this look-up service to identify the standardized term: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/gaz

Slots.name: destination_of_most_recent_travel_state_province_territory
Slots.title: destination of most recent travel (state/province/territory)
Slots.description: The name of the province that was the destination of most recent travel.
Slots.comments: Provide the name of the state/province/territory that the host travelled to. Use this look-up service to identify the standardized term: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/gaz

Slots.name: destination_of_most_recent_travel_country
Slots.title: destination of most recent travel (country)
Slots.description: The name of the country that was the destination of most recent travel.
Slots.comments: Provide the name of the country that the host travelled to. Use this look-up service to identify the standardized term: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/gaz

Slots.name: most_recent_travel_departure_date
Slots.title: most recent travel departure date
Slots.description: The date of a person's most recent departure from their primary residence (at that time) on a journey to one or more other locations.
Slots.comments: Provide the travel departure date.

Slots.name: most_recent_travel_return_date
Slots.title: most recent travel return date
Slots.description: The date of a person's most recent return to some residence from a journey originating at that residence.
Slots.comments: Provide the travel return date.

Slots.name: travel_point_of_entry_type
Slots.title: travel point of entry type
Slots.description: The type of entry point a traveler arrives through.
Slots.comments: Select the point of entry type.

Slots.name: border_testing_test_day_type
Slots.title: border testing test day type
Slots.description: The day a traveller was tested on or after arrival at their point of entry.
Slots.comments: Select the test day.

Slots.name: travel_history
Slots.title: travel history
Slots.description: Travel history in last six months.
Slots.comments: Specify the countries (and more granular locations if known, separated by a comma) travelled in the last six months; can include multiple travels. Separate multiple travel events with a semi-colon. List most recent travel first.

Slots.name: travel_history_availability
Slots.title: travel history availability
Slots.description: The availability of different types of travel history in the last 6 months (e.g. international, domestic).
Slots.comments: If travel history is available, but the details of travel cannot be provided, indicate this and the type of travel history availble by selecting a value from the picklist. The values in this field can be used to indicate a sample is associated with a travel when the "purpose of sequencing" is not travel-associated.

Slots.name: exposure_event
Slots.title: exposure event
Slots.description: Event leading to exposure.
Slots.comments: Select an exposure event from the pick list provided in the template. If the desired term is missing, contact the curation team.

Slots.name: exposure_contact_level
Slots.title: exposure contact level
Slots.description: The exposure transmission contact type.
Slots.comments: Select direct or indirect exposure from the pick-list.

Slots.name: host_role
Slots.title: host role
Slots.description: The role of the host in relation to the exposure setting.
Slots.comments: Select the host's personal role(s) from the pick list provided in the template. If the desired term is missing, contact the curation team.

Slots.name: exposure_setting
Slots.title: exposure setting
Slots.description: The setting leading to exposure.
Slots.comments: Select the host exposure setting(s) from the pick list provided in the template. If a desired term is missing, contact the curation team.

Slots.name: exposure_details
Slots.title: exposure details
Slots.description: Additional host exposure information.
Slots.comments: Free text description of the exposure.

Slots.name: prior_sarscov2_infection
Slots.title: prior SARS-CoV-2 infection
Slots.description: Whether there was prior SARS-CoV-2 infection.
Slots.comments: If known, provide information about whether the individual had a previous SARS-CoV-2 infection. Select a value from the pick list.

Slots.name: prior_sarscov2_infection_isolate
Slots.title: prior SARS-CoV-2 infection isolate
Slots.description: The identifier of the isolate found in the prior SARS-CoV-2 infection.
Slots.comments: Provide the isolate name of the most recent prior infection. Structure the "isolate" name to be ICTV/INSDC compliant in the following format: "SARS-CoV-2/host/country/sampleID/date".

Slots.name: prior_sarscov2_infection_date
Slots.title: prior SARS-CoV-2 infection date
Slots.description: The date of diagnosis of the prior SARS-CoV-2 infection.
Slots.comments: Provide the date that the most recent prior infection was diagnosed. Provide the prior SARS-CoV-2 infection date in ISO 8601 standard format "YYYY-MM-DD".

Slots.name: prior_sarscov2_antiviral_treatment
Slots.title: prior SARS-CoV-2 antiviral treatment
Slots.description: Whether there was prior SARS-CoV-2 treatment with an antiviral agent.
Slots.comments: If known, provide information about whether the individual had a previous SARS-CoV-2 antiviral treatment. Select a value from the pick list.

Slots.name: prior_sarscov2_antiviral_treatment_agent
Slots.title: prior SARS-CoV-2 antiviral treatment agent
Slots.description: The name of the antiviral treatment agent administered during the prior SARS-CoV-2 infection.
Slots.comments: Provide the name of the antiviral treatment agent administered during the most recent prior infection. If no treatment was administered, put "No treatment". If multiple antiviral agents were administered, list them all separated by commas.

Slots.name: prior_sarscov2_antiviral_treatment_date
Slots.title: prior SARS-CoV-2 antiviral treatment date
Slots.description: The date treatment was first administered during the prior SARS-CoV-2 infection.
Slots.comments: Provide the date that the antiviral treatment agent was first administered during the most recenrt prior infection. Provide the prior SARS-CoV-2 treatment date in ISO 8601 standard format "YYYY-MM-DD".

Slots.name: purpose_of_sequencing
Slots.title: purpose of sequencing
Slots.description: The reason that the sample was sequenced.
Slots.comments: The reason why a sample was originally collected may differ from the reason why it was selected for sequencing. The reason a sample was sequenced may provide information about potential biases in sequencing strategy. Provide the purpose of sequencing from the picklist in the template. The reason for sample collection should be indicated in the "purpose of sampling" field.

Slots.name: purpose_of_sequencing_details
Slots.title: purpose of sequencing details
Slots.description: The description of why the sample was sequenced providing specific details.
Slots.comments: Provide an expanded description of why the sample was sequenced using free text. The description may include the importance of the sequences for a particular public health investigation/surveillance activity/research question. Suggested standardized descriotions include: Screened for S gene target failure (S dropout), Screened for mink variants, Screened for B.1.1.7 variant, Screened for B.1.135 variant, Screened for P.1 variant, Screened due to travel history, Screened due to close contact with infected individual, Assessing public health control measures, Determining early introductions and spread, Investigating airline-related exposures, Investigating temporary foreign worker, Investigating remote regions, Investigating health care workers, Investigating schools/universities, Investigating reinfection.
Slots.examples: Screened for S gene target failure (S dropout)

Slots.name: sequencing_date
Slots.title: sequencing date
Slots.description: The date the sample was sequenced.
Slots.comments: ISO 8601 standard "YYYY-MM-DD".

Slots.name: library_id
Slots.title: library ID
Slots.description: The user-specified identifier for the library prepared for sequencing.
Slots.comments: The library name should be unique, and can be an autogenerated ID from your LIMS, or modification of the isolate ID.

Slots.name: amplicon_size
Slots.title: amplicon size
Slots.description: The length of the amplicon generated by PCR amplification.
Slots.comments: Provide the amplicon size, including the units.

Slots.name: library_preparation_kit
Slots.title: library preparation kit
Slots.description: The name of the DNA library preparation kit used to generate the library being sequenced.
Slots.comments: Provide the name of the library preparation kit used.

Slots.name: flow_cell_barcode
Slots.title: flow cell barcode
Slots.description: The barcode of the flow cell used for sequencing.
Slots.comments: Provide the barcode of the flow cell used for sequencing the sample.

Slots.name: sequencing_instrument
Slots.title: sequencing instrument
Slots.description: The model of the sequencing instrument used.
Slots.comments: Select a sequencing instrument from the picklist provided in the template.

Slots.name: sequencing_protocol_name
Slots.title: sequencing protocol name
Slots.description: The name and version number of the sequencing protocol used.
Slots.comments: Provide the name and version of the sequencing protocol e.g. 1D_DNA_MinION

Slots.name: sequencing_protocol
Slots.title: sequencing protocol
Slots.description: The protocol used to generate the sequence.
Slots.comments: Provide a free text description of the methods and materials used to generate the sequence. Suggested text, fill in information where indicated.: "Viral sequencing was performed following a tiling amplicon strategy using the <fill in> primer scheme. Sequencing was performed using a <fill in> sequencing instrument. Libraries were prepared using <fill in> library kit. "
Slots.examples: Genomes were generated through amplicon sequencing of 1200 bp amplicons with Freed schema primers. Libraries were created using Illumina DNA Prep kits, and sequence data was produced using Miseq Micro v2 (500 cycles) sequencing kits.

Slots.name: sequencing_kit_number
Slots.title: sequencing kit number
Slots.description: The manufacturer's kit number.
Slots.comments: Alphanumeric value.

Slots.name: amplicon_pcr_primer_scheme
Slots.title: amplicon pcr primer scheme
Slots.description: The specifications of the primers (primer sequences, binding positions, fragment size generated etc) used to generate the amplicons to be sequenced.
Slots.comments: Provide the name and version of the primer scheme used to generate the amplicons for sequencing.

Slots.name: raw_sequence_data_processing_method
Slots.title: raw sequence data processing method
Slots.description: The names of the software and version number used for raw data processing such as removing barcodes, adapter trimming, filtering etc.
Slots.comments: Provide the software name followed by the version e.g. Trimmomatic v. 0.38, Porechop v. 0.2.3

Slots.name: dehosting_method
Slots.title: dehosting method
Slots.description: The method used to remove host reads from the pathogen sequence.
Slots.comments: Provide the name and version number of the software used to remove host reads.

Slots.name: consensus_sequence_name
Slots.title: consensus sequence name
Slots.description: The name of the consensus sequence.
Slots.comments: Provide the name and version number of the consensus sequence.

Slots.name: consensus_sequence_filename
Slots.title: consensus sequence filename
Slots.description: The name of the consensus sequence file.
Slots.comments: Provide the name and version number of the consensus sequence FASTA file.

Slots.name: consensus_sequence_filepath
Slots.title: consensus sequence filepath
Slots.description: The filepath of the consensus sequence file.
Slots.comments: Provide the filepath of the consensus sequence FASTA file.

Slots.name: consensus_sequence_software_name
Slots.title: consensus sequence software name
Slots.description: The name of software used to generate the consensus sequence.
Slots.comments: Provide the name of the software used to generate the consensus sequence.

Slots.name: consensus_sequence_software_version
Slots.title: consensus sequence software version
Slots.description: The version of the software used to generate the consensus sequence.
Slots.comments: Provide the version of the software used to generate the consensus sequence.

Slots.name: breadth_of_coverage_value
Slots.title: breadth of coverage value
Slots.description: The percentage of the reference genome covered by the sequenced data, to a prescribed depth.
Slots.comments: Provide value as a percent.

Slots.name: depth_of_coverage_value
Slots.title: depth of coverage value
Slots.description: The average number of reads representing a given nucleotide in the reconstructed sequence.
Slots.comments: Provide value as a fold of coverage.

Slots.name: depth_of_coverage_threshold
Slots.title: depth of coverage threshold
Slots.description: The threshold used as a cut-off for the depth of coverage.
Slots.comments: Provide the threshold fold coverage.

Slots.name: r1_fastq_filename
Slots.title: r1 fastq filename
Slots.description: The user-specified filename of the r1 FASTQ file.
Slots.comments: Provide the r1 FASTQ filename.

Slots.name: r2_fastq_filename
Slots.title: r2 fastq filename
Slots.description: The user-specified filename of the r2 FASTQ file.
Slots.comments: Provide the r2 FASTQ filename.

Slots.name: r1_fastq_filepath
Slots.title: r1 fastq filepath
Slots.description: The location of the r1 FASTQ file within a user's file system.
Slots.comments: Provide the filepath for the r1 FASTQ file. This information aids in data management.

Slots.name: r2_fastq_filepath
Slots.title: r2 fastq filepath
Slots.description: The location of the r2 FASTQ file within a user's file system.
Slots.comments: Provide the filepath for the r2 FASTQ file. This information aids in data management.

Slots.name: fast5_filename
Slots.title: fast5 filename
Slots.description: The user-specified filename of the FAST5 file.
Slots.comments: Provide the FAST5 filename.

Slots.name: fast5_filepath
Slots.title: fast5 filepath
Slots.description: The location of the FAST5 file within a user's file system.
Slots.comments: Provide the filepath for the FAST5 file. This information aids in data management.

Slots.name: number_of_base_pairs_sequenced
Slots.title: number of base pairs sequenced
Slots.description: The number of total base pairs generated by the sequencing process.
Slots.comments: Provide a numerical value (no need to include units).

Slots.name: consensus_genome_length
Slots.title: consensus genome length
Slots.description: Size of the reconstructed genome described as the number of base pairs.
Slots.comments: Provide a numerical value (no need to include units).

Slots.name: ns_per_100_kbp
Slots.title: Ns per 100 kbp
Slots.description: The number of N symbols present in the consensus fasta sequence, per 100kbp of sequence.
Slots.comments: Provide a numerical value (no need to include units).

Slots.name: reference_genome_accession
Slots.title: reference genome accession
Slots.description: A persistent, unique identifier of a genome database entry.
Slots.comments: Provide the accession number of the reference genome.

Slots.name: bioinformatics_protocol
Slots.title: bioinformatics protocol
Slots.description: A description of the overall bioinformatics strategy used.
Slots.comments: Further details regarding the methods used to process raw data, and/or generate assemblies, and/or generate consensus sequences can. This information can be provided in an SOP or protocol or pipeline/workflow. Provide the name and version number of the protocol, or a GitHub link to a pipeline or workflow.

Slots.name: lineage_clade_name
Slots.title: lineage/clade name
Slots.description: The name of the lineage or clade.
Slots.comments: Provide the Pangolin or Nextstrain lineage/clade name.

Slots.name: lineage_clade_analysis_software_name
Slots.title: lineage/clade analysis software name
Slots.description: The name of the software used to determine the lineage/clade.
Slots.comments: Provide the name of the software used to determine the lineage/clade.

Slots.name: lineage_clade_analysis_software_version
Slots.title: lineage/clade analysis software version
Slots.description: The version of the software used to determine the lineage/clade.
Slots.comments: Provide the version of the software used ot determine the lineage/clade.

Slots.name: variant_designation
Slots.title: variant designation
Slots.description: The variant classification of the lineage/clade i.e. variant, variant of concern.
Slots.comments: If the lineage/clade is considered a Variant of Concern, select Variant of Concern from the pick list. If the lineage/clade contains mutations of concern (mutations that increase transmission, clincal severity, or other epidemiological fa ctors) but it not a global Variant of Concern, select Variant. If the lineage/clade does not contain mutations of concern, leave blank.

Slots.name: variant_evidence
Slots.title: variant evidence
Slots.description: The evidence used to make the variant determination.
Slots.comments: Select whether the sample was screened using RT-qPCR or by sequencing from the pick list.

Slots.name: variant_evidence_details
Slots.title: variant evidence details
Slots.description: Details about the evidence used to make the variant determination.
Slots.comments: Provide the assay and list the set of lineage-defining mutations used to make the variant determination. If there are mutations of interest/concern observed in addition to lineage-defining mutations, describe those here.
Slots.examples: Lineage-defining mutations: ORF1ab (K1655N), Spike (K417N, E484K, N501Y, D614G, A701V), N (T205I), E (P71L).

Slots.name: gene_name_1
Slots.title: gene name 1
Slots.description: The name of the gene used in the diagnostic RT-PCR test.
Slots.comments: Provide the full name of the gene used in the test. The gene symbol (short form of gene name) can also be provided. Standardized gene names and symbols can be found in the Gene Ontology using this look-up service: https://bit.ly/2Sq1LbI

Slots.name: diagnostic_pcr_protocol_1
Slots.title: diagnostic pcr protocol 1
Slots.description: The name and version number of the protocol used for diagnostic marker amplification.
Slots.comments: The name and version number of the protocol used for carrying out a diagnostic PCR test. This information can be compared to sequence data for evaluation of performance and quality control.

Slots.name: diagnostic_pcr_ct_value_1
Slots.title: diagnostic pcr Ct value 1
Slots.description: The Ct value result from a diagnostic SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR test.
Slots.comments: Provide the CT value of the sample from the diagnostic RT-PCR test.

Slots.name: gene_name_2
Slots.title: gene name 2
Slots.description: The name of the gene used in the diagnostic RT-PCR test.
Slots.comments: Provide the full name of another gene used in an RT-PCR test. The gene symbol (short form of gene name) can also be provided. Standardized gene names and symbols can be found in the Gene Ontology using this look-up service: https://bit.ly/2Sq1LbI

Slots.name: diagnostic_pcr_protocol_2
Slots.title: diagnostic pcr protocol 2
Slots.description: The name and version number of the protocol used for diagnostic marker amplification.
Slots.comments: The name and version number of the protocol used for carrying out a second diagnostic PCR test. This information can be compared to sequence data for evaluation of performance and quality control.

Slots.name: diagnostic_pcr_ct_value_2
Slots.title: diagnostic pcr Ct value 2
Slots.description: The Ct value result from a diagnostic SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR test.
Slots.comments: Provide the CT value of the sample from the second diagnostic RT-PCR test.

Slots.name: gene_name_3
Slots.title: gene name 3
Slots.description: The name of the gene used in the diagnostic RT-PCR test.
Slots.comments: Provide the full name of another gene used in an RT-PCR test. The gene symbol (short form of gene name) can also be provided. Standardized gene names and symbols can be found in the Gene Ontology using this look-up service: https://bit.ly/2Sq1LbI

Slots.name: diagnostic_pcr_protocol_3
Slots.title: diagnostic pcr protocol 3
Slots.description: The name and version number of the protocol used for diagnostic marker amplification.
Slots.comments: The name and version number of the protocol used for carrying out a second diagnostic PCR test. This information can be compared to sequence data for evaluation of performance and quality control.

Slots.name: diagnostic_pcr_ct_value_3
Slots.title: diagnostic pcr Ct value 3
Slots.description: The Ct value result from a diagnostic SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR test.
Slots.comments: Provide the CT value of the sample from the second diagnostic RT-PCR test.

Slots.name: authors
Slots.title: authors
Slots.description: Names of individuals contributing to the processes of sample collection, sequence generation, analysis, and data submission.
Slots.comments: Include the first and last names of all individuals that should be attributed, separated by a comma.
Slots.examples: Tejinder Singh, Fei Hu, Joe Blogs

Slots.name: dataharmonizer_provenance
Slots.title: DataHarmonizer provenance
Slots.description: The DataHarmonizer software and template version provenance.
Slots.comments: The current software and template version information will be automatically generated in this field after the user utilizes the "validate" function. This information will be generated regardless as to whether the row is valid of not.

Slots.name: specimen_collector_sample_id
Slots.title: specimen collector sample ID
Slots.description: The user-defined name for the sample.
Slots.comments: Store the collector sample ID. If this number is considered identifiable information, provide an alternative ID. Be sure to store the key that maps between the original and alternative IDs for traceability and follow up if necessary. Every collector sample ID from a single submitter must be unique. It can have any format, but we suggest that you make it concise, unique and consistent within your lab.

Slots.name: third_party_lab_service_provider_name
Slots.title: third party lab service provider name
Slots.description: The name of the third party company or laboratory that provided services.
Slots.comments: Provide the full, unabbreviated name of the company or laboratory.

Slots.name: third_party_lab_sample_id
Slots.title: third party lab sample ID
Slots.description: The identifier assigned to a sample by a third party service provider.
Slots.comments: Store the sample identifier supplied by the third party services provider.

Slots.name: case_id
Slots.title: case ID
Slots.description: The identifier used to specify an epidemiologically detected case of disease.
Slots.comments: Provide the case identifer. The case ID greatly facilitates linkage between laboratory and epidemiological data. The case ID may be considered identifiable information. Consult the data steward before sharing.

Slots.name: related_specimen_primary_id
Slots.title: Related specimen primary ID
Slots.description: The primary ID of a related specimen previously submitted to the repository.
Slots.comments: Store the primary ID of the related specimen previously submitted to the National Microbiology Laboratory so that the samples can be linked and tracked through the system.

Slots.name: irida_sample_name
Slots.title: IRIDA sample name
Slots.description: The identifier assigned to a sequenced isolate in IRIDA.
Slots.comments: Store the IRIDA sample name. The IRIDA sample name will be created by the individual entering data into the IRIDA platform. IRIDA samples may be linked to metadata and sequence data, or just metadata alone. It is recommended that the IRIDA sample name be the same as, or contain, the specimen collector sample ID for better traceability. It is also recommended that the IRIDA sample name mirror the GISAID accession. IRIDA sample names cannot contain slashes. Slashes should be replaced by underscores. See IRIDA documentation for more information regarding special characters (https://irida.corefacility.ca/documentation/user/user/samples/#adding-a-new-sample).

Slots.name: umbrella_bioproject_accession
Slots.title: umbrella bioproject accession
Slots.description: The INSDC accession number assigned to the umbrella BioProject for the Canadian SARS-CoV-2 sequencing effort.
Slots.comments: Store the umbrella BioProject accession by selecting it from the picklist in the template. The umbrella BioProject accession will be identical for all CanCOGen submitters. Different provinces will have their own BioProjects, however these BioProjects will be linked under one umbrella BioProject.

Slots.name: bioproject_accession
Slots.title: bioproject accession
Slots.description: The INSDC accession number of the BioProject(s) to which the BioSample belongs.
Slots.comments: Store the BioProject accession number. BioProjects are an organizing tool that links together raw sequence data, assemblies, and their associated metadata. Each province will be assigned a different bioproject accession number by the National Microbiology Lab. A valid NCBI BioProject accession has prefix PRJN e.g., PRJNA12345, and is created once at the beginning of a new sequencing project.

Slots.name: biosample_accession
Slots.title: biosample accession
Slots.description: The identifier assigned to a BioSample in INSDC archives.
Slots.comments: Store the accession returned from the BioSample submission. NCBI BioSamples will have the prefix SAMN.

Slots.name: sra_accession
Slots.title: SRA accession
Slots.description: The Sequence Read Archive (SRA) identifier linking raw read data, methodological metadata and quality control metrics submitted to the INSDC.
Slots.comments: Store the accession assigned to the submitted "run". NCBI-SRA accessions start with SRR.

Slots.name: genbank_accession
Slots.title: GenBank accession
Slots.description: The GenBank identifier assigned to the sequence in the INSDC archives.
Slots.comments: Store the accession returned from a GenBank submission (viral genome assembly).

Slots.name: gisaid_accession
Slots.title: GISAID accession
Slots.description: The GISAID accession number assigned to the sequence.
Slots.comments: Store the accession returned from the GISAID submission.

Slots.name: sample_collected_by
Slots.title: sample collected by
Slots.description: The name of the agency that collected the original sample.
Slots.comments: The name of the sample collector should be written out in full, (with minor exceptions) and be consistent across multple submissions e.g. Public Health Agency of Canada, Public Health Ontario, BC Centre for Disease Control. The sample collector specified is at the discretion of the data provider (i.e. may be hospital, provincial public health lab, or other).

Slots.name: sample_collector_contact_email
Slots.title: sample collector contact email
Slots.description: The email address of the contact responsible for follow-up regarding the sample.
Slots.comments: The email address can represent a specific individual or lab e.g. johnnyblogs@lab.ca, or RespLab@lab.ca

Slots.name: sample_collector_contact_address
Slots.title: sample collector contact address
Slots.description: The mailing address of the agency submitting the sample.
Slots.comments: The mailing address should be in the format: Street number and name, City, Province/Territory, Postal Code, Country
Slots.examples: 655 Lab St, Vancouver, British Columbia, V5N 2A2, Canada

Slots.name: sequence_submitted_by
Slots.title: sequence submitted by
Slots.description: The name of the agency that generated the sequence.
Slots.comments: The name of the agency should be written out in full, (with minor exceptions) and be consistent across multple submissions. If submitting specimens rather than sequencing data, please put the "National Microbiology Laboratory (NML)".

Slots.name: sequence_submitter_contact_email
Slots.title: sequence submitter contact email
Slots.description: The email address of the contact responsible for follow-up regarding the sequence.
Slots.comments: The email address can represent a specific individual or lab e.g. johnnyblogs@lab.ca, or RespLab@lab.ca

Slots.name: sequence_submitter_contact_address
Slots.title: sequence submitter contact address
Slots.description: The mailing address of the agency submitting the sequence.
Slots.comments: The mailing address should be in the format: Street number and name, City, Province/Territory, Postal Code, Country
Slots.examples: 123 Sunnybrooke St, Toronto, Ontario, M4P 1L6, Canada

Slots.name: sample_collection_date
Slots.title: sample collection date
Slots.description: The date on which the sample was collected.
Slots.comments: Sample collection date is critical for surveillance and many types of analyses. Required granularity includes year, month and day. If this date is considered identifiable information, it is acceptable to add "jitter" by adding or subtracting a calendar day (acceptable by GISAID). Alternatively, ”received date” may be used as a substitute. The date should be provided in ISO 8601 standard format "YYYY-MM-DD".

Slots.name: sample_collection_date_precision
Slots.title: sample collection date precision
Slots.description: The precision to which the "sample collection date" was provided.
Slots.comments: Provide the precision of granularity to the "day", "month", or "year" for the date provided in the "sample collection date" field. The "sample collection date" will be truncated to the precision specified upon export: "day" for "YYYY-MM-DD", "month" for "YYYY-MM", or "year" for "YYYY".

Slots.name: sample_received_date
Slots.title: sample received date
Slots.description: The date on which the sample was received.
Slots.comments: ISO 8601 standard "YYYY-MM-DD".

Slots.name: geo_loc_name_country
Slots.title: geo_loc_name (country)
Slots.description: The country where the sample was collected.
Slots.comments: Provide the country name from the controlled vocabulary provided.

Slots.name: geo_loc_name_state_province_territory
Slots.title: geo_loc_name (state/province/territory)
Slots.description: The province/territory where the sample was collected.
Slots.comments: Provide the province/territory name from the controlled vocabulary provided.

Slots.name: geo_loc_name_city
Slots.title: geo_loc_name (city)
Slots.description: The city where the sample was collected.
Slots.comments: Provide the city name. Use this look-up service to identify the standardized term: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/gaz

Slots.name: organism
Slots.title: organism
Slots.description: Taxonomic name of the organism.
Slots.comments: Use "Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2". This value is provided in the template.

Slots.name: isolate
Slots.title: isolate
Slots.description: Identifier of the specific isolate.
Slots.comments: Provide the GISAID virus name, which should be written in the format “hCov-19/CANADA/2 digit provincial ISO code-xxxxx/year”.

Slots.name: purpose_of_sampling
Slots.title: purpose of sampling
Slots.description: The reason that the sample was collected.
Slots.comments: The reason a sample was collected may provide information about potential biases in sampling strategy. Provide the purpose of sampling from the picklist in the template. Most likely, the sample was collected for diagnostic testing. The reason why a sample was originally collected may differ from the reason why it was selected for sequencing, which should be indicated in the "purpose of sequencing" field.

Slots.name: purpose_of_sampling_details
Slots.title: purpose of sampling details
Slots.description: The description of why the sample was collected, providing specific details.
Slots.comments: Provide an expanded description of why the sample was collected using free text. The description may include the importance of the sample for a particular public health investigation/surveillance activity/research question. If details are not available, provide a null value.
Slots.examples: The sample was collected to investigate the prevalence of variants associated with mink-to-human transmission in Canada.

Slots.name: nml_submitted_specimen_type
Slots.title: NML submitted specimen type
Slots.description: The type of specimen submitted to the National Microbiology Laboratory (NML) for testing.
Slots.comments: This information is required for upload through the CNPHI LaSER system. Select the specimen type from the pick list provided. If sequence data is being submitted rather than a specimen for testing, select “Not Applicable”.

Slots.name: related_specimen_relationship_type
Slots.title: Related specimen relationship type
Slots.description: The relationship of the current specimen to the specimen/sample previously submitted to the repository.
Slots.comments: Provide the tag that describes how the previous sample is related to the current sample being submitted from the pick list provided, so that the samples can be linked and tracked in the system.

Slots.name: anatomical_material
Slots.title: anatomical material
Slots.description: A substance obtained from an anatomical part of an organism e.g. tissue, blood.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if an anatomical material was sampled. Use the picklist provided in the template. If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: anatomical_part
Slots.title: anatomical part
Slots.description: An anatomical part of an organism e.g. oropharynx.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if an anatomical part was sampled. Use the picklist provided in the template. If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: body_product
Slots.title: body product
Slots.description: A substance excreted/secreted from an organism e.g. feces, urine, sweat.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if a body product was sampled. Use the picklist provided in the template.  If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: environmental_material
Slots.title: environmental material
Slots.description: A substance obtained from the natural or man-made environment e.g. soil, water, sewage.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if an environmental material was sampled. Use the picklist provided in the template.  If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: environmental_site
Slots.title: environmental site
Slots.description: An environmental location may describe a site in the natural or built environment e.g. contact surface, metal can, hospital, wet market, bat cave.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if an environmental site was sampled. Use the picklist provided in the template.  If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: collection_device
Slots.title: collection device
Slots.description: The instrument or container used to collect the sample e.g. swab.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if a device was used for sampling. Use the picklist provided in the template. If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: collection_method
Slots.title: collection method
Slots.description: The process used to collect the sample e.g. phlebotomy, necropsy.
Slots.comments: Provide a descriptor if a collection method was used for sampling. Use the picklist provided in the template.  If a desired term is missing from the picklist, contact emma_griffiths@sfu.ca. If not applicable, do not leave blank. Choose a null value.

Slots.name: collection_protocol
Slots.title: collection protocol
Slots.description: The name and version of a particular protocol used for sampling.
Slots.comments: Free text.

Slots.name: specimen_processing
Slots.title: specimen processing
Slots.description: Any processing applied to the sample during or after receiving the sample.
Slots.comments: Critical for interpreting data. Select all the applicable processes from the pick list. If virus was passaged, include information in "lab host", "passage number", and "passage method" fields. If none of the processes in the pick list apply, put "not applicable".

Slots.name: specimen_processing_details
Slots.title: specimen processing details
Slots.description: Detailed information regarding the processing applied to a sample during or after receiving the sample.
Slots.comments: Provide a free text description of any processing details applied to a sample.
Slots.examples: 25 swabs were pooled and further prepared as a single sample during library prep.

Slots.name: lab_host
Slots.title: lab host
Slots.description: Name and description of the laboratory host used to propagate the source organism or material from which the sample was obtained.
Slots.comments: Type of cell line used for propagation. Provide the name of the cell line using the picklist in the template. If not passaged, put "not applicable".

Slots.name: passage_number
Slots.title: passage number
Slots.description: Number of passages.
Slots.comments: Provide number of known passages. If not passaged, put "not applicable"

Slots.name: passage_method
Slots.title: passage method
Slots.description: Description of how organism was passaged.
Slots.comments: Free text. Provide a very short description (<10 words). If not passaged, put "not applicable".

Slots.name: biomaterial_extracted
Slots.title: biomaterial extracted
Slots.description: The biomaterial extracted from samples for the purpose of sequencing.
Slots.comments: Provide the biomaterial extracted from the picklist in the template.

Slots.name: host_common_name
Slots.title: host (common name)
Slots.description: The commonly used name of the host.
Slots.comments: Common name or scientific name are required if there was a host. Both can be provided, if known. Use terms from the pick lists in the template. Common name e.g. human, bat. If the sample was environmental, put "not applicable.

Slots.name: host_scientific_name
Slots.title: host (scientific name)
Slots.description: The taxonomic, or scientific name of the host.
Slots.comments: Common name or scientific name are required if there was a host. Both can be provided, if known. Use terms from the pick lists in the template. Scientific name e.g. Homo sapiens, If the sample was environmental, put "not applicable

Slots.name: host_health_state
Slots.title: host health state
Slots.description: Health status of the host at the time of sample collection.
Slots.comments: If known, select a descriptor from the pick list provided in the template.

Slots.name: host_health_status_details
Slots.title: host health status details
Slots.description: Further details pertaining to the health or disease status of the host at time of collection.
Slots.comments: If known, select a descriptor from the pick list provided in the template.

Slots.name: host_health_outcome
Slots.title: host health outcome
Slots.description: Disease outcome in the host.
Slots.comments: If known, select a descriptor from the pick list provided in the template.

Slots.name: host_disease
Slots.title: host disease
Slots.description: The name of the disease experienced by the host.
Slots.comments: Select "COVID-19" from the pick list provided in the template.

Slots.name: host_age
Slots.title: host age
Slots.description: Age of host at the time of sampling.
Slots.comments: Enter the age of the host in years. If not available, provide a null value. If there is not host, put "Not Applicable".

Slots.name: host_age_unit
Slots.title: host age unit
Slots.description: The unit used to measure the host age, in either months or years.
Slots.comments: Indicate whether the host age is in months or years. Age indicated in months will be binned to the 0 - 9 year age bin.
